required_fixes: Add an explicit statement identifying the related financial statements (eg, consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024) and confirm the sustainability disclosures are for the same reporting entity (IFRS_S1_20_C01, IFRS_S1_22_C01).

Strengthen connected information by providing specific linkages/cross-references between sustainability disclosures and the financial statements (eg, where climate-related capex, provisions/impairments, or risk disclosures are reflected) rather than only stating currency consistency (IFRS_S1_21_C04).

Either (a) include the required disclosures about all sustainability-related risks and opportunities affecting prospects (beyond climate), or (b) clearly scope this section as basis-of-preparation only and ensure the full report elsewhere meets IFRS_S1_3_C01 (IFRS_S1_3_C01).

Disclose the specific external standards/guidance applied (eg, IFRS S1/S2, SASB topics considered, NGFS, PCAF) and the industry classification used to identify applicable metrics; explicitly state SASB topics/metrics were considered (or not applicable) (IFRS_S1_55_C01, IFRS_S1_58_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C02).

Add disclosures describing how the Bank determines which IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard specifically applies to each risk/opportunity and how judgement is applied when none applies, including how relevance and faithful representation are ensured (IFRS_S1_56_C01, IFRS_S1_57_C01, IFRS_S1_57_C02).
State whether information is incorporated by cross-reference to other reports; if yes, include the cross-reference mechanics consistent with B45–B47 (IFRS_S1_63_C01).
State that sustainability-related financial disclosures are reported at the same time as the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_64_C01).

If relying on the 'additional information' principle, identify at least one concrete example where additional information was necessary and provided to explain effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital (IFRS_S1_15_C02).

required_fixes.fix: Add/replace evidence linkage for fiscal year-end date to bank.fiscal_year_end (or equivalent audited financial statements reference) for the statement 'fiscal year ends on 31 December 2024' (GR-005).
Add/replace evidence linkage for reporting currency to bank.reporting_currency (or financial statements note) for 'reporting currency is EUR' (GR-006).
Provide a concrete evidence source for 'green loans 10.71%' (e.g., reporting_kpis.green_loans_pct_2024 or taxonomy/portfolio KPI table) and cite it for GR-032.
Clean up evidence mappings where unrelated sources are cited (e.g., remove board_climate_expertise_pct from GR-012 unless it truly supports the 69.8% agenda metric).
For Table 1 data quality percentages, cite evidence paths for each percentage (estimated/proxy/audited) or a single structured object that contains all four values.

For Scope 1/2 totals, cite the specific emissions inventory/KPI fields that contain those totals (rather than scope2 reconciliation narrative or generic target progress fields), and ensure location-based vs market-based are separately evidenced.

required_fixes: Remove or generalize hard-coded reporting years, specific dates, currencies, and jurisdiction lists from template-style narrative. Replace with configurable placeholders or generic wording (e.g., 'the reporting period', 'the reporting currency', 'relevant jurisdictions') to comply with the 'what_to_avoid' rules.

Refocus the section on basis of preparation and 'how to read this report' mechanics by removing or relocating detailed performance metrics (e.g., financed emissions, capex, Tier 1 capital, Scope 1/2/3 values, green loans percentage) to the dedicated Metrics and Targets section, and instead include cross-references (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Metrics and Targets]').

Introduce or refine one-sentence purpose statements at the start of each subsection that explicitly state what the subsection describes (e.g., 'This subsection describes the reporting period applied to these sustainability-related financial disclosures.').

Add closing connectivity sentences to major subsections (e.g., 1.1, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.8, 1.9) that link to related sections or the financial statements using generic cross-reference placeholders (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance]' or 'See [Related Financial Statements]').

Separate high-level principles from detailed mechanics in methodology subsections. For example, in 1.6, first state the overarching principles for climate-related methodologies, then use bullets or short paragraphs for specific methods (risk rating, scenario analysis, emissions accounting) without embedding detailed case examples unless clearly labelled as illustrative.

Simplify and standardize wording to use preferred standards-oriented verbs and cautious modality. Replace narrative verbs like 'explains' and 'sets out' with 'describes', 'presents', 'discloses', and ensure judgement-heavy areas use 'may', 'could', or 'is subject to'.
Review long or multi-clause sentences and split them into shorter, single-idea sentences to improve clarity and align with the sentence_length guidance.

Adjust numeric precision to a reasonable number of decimal places consistent with audit-ready practice (e.g., one or two decimals for emissions and intensity metrics) and state rounding conventions where relevant.

Enhance the data quality and estimates sections to more explicitly distinguish between current-period facts, estimates/judgements, and any forward-looking intentions, and, where any data is incomplete or estimated, follow the missing_data_language_rules (what is missing, why, interim approach, limitations, and planned enhancements).

Consider adding a compact mapping table that links each general requirement topic (e.g., reporting boundary, comparatives, connected information) to the sections where detailed disclosures appear, to improve navigability and align with the preferred table usage for this section.

approval_policy: V9.1: deterministic evidence/fact gates are binding; style judge is advisory unless IFRS_STYLE_JUDGE_MODE=blocking.

section_generation_score.policy: Missing requirements reduce audit/readiness visibility only; they must not appear in report prose.
